claims.statement: The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive calls for one-stop shops that support owners, SMEs, installers and financial actors through renovation.
The Directive identifies mechanisms addressing upfront renovation costs, including pay-as-you-save and energy-performance contracting.

Polish consumer-credit intermediation has an obtainable registration route: KNF states that activity may begin after entry in the register, with a 600 PLN application fee and a 14-day entry period for complete and correct documentation.
Credit Agricole already distributes OZE credit through installer partners: the installer helps with the application and the bank pays the financed amount to the installation company.
BNP Paribas offers a current retail credit product for OZE equipment through participating stores and explicitly recruits stores to intermediate the credit agreement.

Inbank reported more than 200 Polish OZE distribution and installation partners, more than 80,000 prior green-installation loans, and a commitment to provide over 700 million PLN of new green loans over three years.
Energa and SGB already market an integrated path from energy-project advice through bank financing and implementation, including solutions for firms, farms and multi-unit housing.

The evidence supports a real embedded-finance behavior but also shows that the household OZE version of the proposed channel is mature; an independent router would need a narrower commercial-building workflow or superior multi-lender conversion economics.

contrary_evidence: The Directive creates policy direction, not a lender partnership, borrower demand or permission for the proposed intermediary activity.
Credit Agricole, BNP Paribas and Inbank already place credit inside installer or merchant sales flows, so exclusive placement is neither novel nor evidenced as available.
Energa and SGB already combine technical delivery and financing in one customer journey, showing that large utilities and banks can bypass a neutral router.
The enhanced BGK thermomodernisation grant had a 30 June 2026 application cutoff, illustrating that policy-linked acquisition wedges can change or expire.

economics.acquisition_route: Research update: pilot through the family renewable-energy company remains a credible test route, but household installer finance is already distributed by bank-partner networks and integrated energy providers. The unvalidated wedge is therefore smaller commercial-building projects or multi-lender document orchestration that incumbent single-lender flows do not serve.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: fund 100 projects in year 1, reach 2 million PLN annual revenue by year 3, 3.5 million PLN founder-owned equity and retained cash by year 5, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 6-9. Research found no evidence for the assumed funded-project volume, fee rate or valuation path.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-3 hours per day only after lender compliance, installer onboarding and exception support are documented and delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 65%-85% gross margin was not substantiated because no lender commission schedule, integration cost or exception-support burden was public.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 9-18 months depends on lender-paid economics and funded conversion that remain unknown; mature incumbent channels may increase integration and acquisition cost.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: proposed lender-paid fee of 1%-3% of funded principal and installer software fee of 300-900 PLN per month. Public bank pages disclose borrower terms but not partner commissions or willingness to pay a neutral router.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat could follow every qualified quote, but installer retention, multi-lender usage and exclusivity are not evidenced.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented quote, asset, approval and funding outcomes improve lender routing and make the channel more valuable
fingerprint.customer: SME energy-renovation installers and their commercial-building customers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Exclusive installer and quoting-platform integrations at the moment of purchase
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Quote-embedded finance matching and document orchestration without holding credit risk
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A regulated lender pays after a referred financing agreement is funded; an installer may also pay for workflow software
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A technically acceptable retrofit quote stalls because the buyer cannot or will not pay upfront

founder_fit: Starts with a real installer test bed.
Uses finance, data science and automation skills.
Avoids lending balance-sheet risk if structured correctly.
The registration and compliance work can be delegated to counsel, while the founder can run a bounded family-business pilot without becoming a public-facing salesperson.
risks: Regulatory perimeter or consumer-credit rules may apply.
A lender can terminate the channel or copy the integration.
Poor underwriting outcomes could damage installer trust.
Banks and energy incumbents already own installer or merchant channels and may decline neutral routing or exclusivity.
Policy-program changes can invalidate an acquisition script or project-eligibility workflow.

structure.control_point: Exclusive placement inside installer quotes plus contractual access to consented application and funding-outcome data
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed lending partner and a legal structure that keeps the company outside regulated lending and unauthorised intermediation

thesis: Give small Polish retrofit installers a white-label financing router embedded in their quote, while regulated lenders retain underwriting and lending. Exclusive installer-channel agreements and consented quote-to-funding performance data create a distribution and matching moat; revenue comes from completed finance, not generic lead resale.
title: Installer-Owned Retrofit Finance Rail
uncertainties: Commission economics offered by Polish lenders
Funding conversion and consented data rights
Whether commercial-building retrofit tickets are frequent enough and underserved relative to mature household OZE finance
Exact consumer-credit, mortgage-credit and business-credit perimeter for each proposed customer and activity
